issue.title: reverse default for cascade_backrefs flag

labels.name: alchemy 2
labels.description: goes along with the 2.0 milestone to aid in searching

issue.body: as discussed in #5130, and also regarding similar confusion in #5149, cascade_backrefs behavior should be on all the time and we should reverse the default for this.     warning in 1.4 will be that when cascade_backrefs behavior actually occurs, a removedin20 warning is emitted.

body:
there are a bunch of things going on here and it is not clear if further action is warranted:

1. the test case here will behave differently in 1.4, due to #4993 , where there are no longer any persistence-related cascades on the "boston_addresses" relationship

2. when you emit `Address(user=user, city='Boston')`, and then you expect user.boston_addresses to have entries inside of it, there are some assumptions going on here that SQLAlchemy is likely going to change, as a result of, OK forgot to add the ticket for this, here it is, #5150.   Basically you made an `Address()` and pointed it to the persistent user.   By backref rules, that means the address is appended to the user.boston_addresses list, which is already an issue because you've labeled this as viewonly=True and it just got mutated.  however, if you then expect "address" to be present in the Session in preparation for persistence, that only occurs due to the user.boston_addresses append.  This is where backrefs confuse everyone, in that they move objects into the Session when you didn't actually "put" them anywhere.   That will reverse due to #5150, as well as due to #4993 which will turn off the save-update cascade for viewonly.

Basically the test case in 1.4 will look like this:


```
    address = Address(user=user, city='Boston')

    # did not add address to the session
    assert address not in session

    # it's in user.boston_addresses due to back_populates,
    # but this does not imply DB persitence
    assert user.boston_addresses == [address]

    # persist to the DB and expire (similar to session.commit())
    session.flush()
    session.expire_all()

    # Address was not persisted because it was never added to the
    # session, collection is empty
    assert user.boston_addresses == []

```

so what can we do here except perhaps warn that "back_populates" doesn't make sense with viewonly=True, because, it's viewonly, and nothing is supposed to be appended to it.   I think that might be where we have to go here.    will try that.
this should be warn in 1.4 and possible 1.3.x as well.  2.0 should disallow.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Begin to disallow back_populates with viewonly=True** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/1719

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_1_3** branch:

**Begin to disallow back_populates with viewonly=True** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/1720

rename.from: Duplicates in relationship list when back_populates refers to viewonly relationship

rename.to: warn and deprecate for back_populates with viewonly=True

body:
Thanks for your swift and thorough analysis!

I agree that my setup was fishy, it was deduced from a much more complex setup that eventually boiled down to this.

I may be wrong, but I think that we’re losing an important use case here, which is introspection of inverse relationships. I would recommend allowing the backref IFF the backref is also view_only.


(Also commented on bitbucket, but I think here is more appropriate; sorry for double-posting.)

@maparent  the sourcecode for SQLAlchemy is right in this github repo, you can comment here.

Show me a code example illustrating the introspection of inverse case you are referring towards, thanks.

I can show you in my own code, but it's very idiosyncratic: for example 
https://github.com/conversence/idealoom/blob/cfa59684f638446e228b9e6337ee13ffbb0dc22b/assembl/views/traversal.py#L880 or https://github.com/conversence/idealoom/blob/cfa59684f638446e228b9e6337ee13ffbb0dc22b/assembl/lib/sqla.py#L1429.
I'm starting to add my backrefs to info so I can navigate back and forth, as in https://github.com/conversence/idealoom/blob/cfa59684f638446e228b9e6337ee13ffbb0dc22b/assembl/models/idea.py#L1710
But rather than justify my code, I'm realizing that a broader argument can be made: Anytime we have a many-to-many relationship with a non-trivial join table, it makes sense to forbid direct manipulation (because the join table rows should be created explicitly) but we may still want a view_only relationship for convenient navigation through the join. Being able to simply declare a backref in this case remains convenient, though I agree totally the backref should also be view_only.
Best regards,
Marc-Antoine Parent

I dont like "backref()" either and it's been superseded by back_populates which is more explciit and less misleading.   "backref()" isnt going away but it's not the best practice now.

there is no option to restore the back_populates flag for viewonly because it implies a mutating behavior.    trying to guess that both sides (noting there can be more than two sides in inheriting scenarios) are "viewonly" is not worth the complexity and nor does it really make sense because again back_populates is about mutations of attributes.    if you want some notational feature for some highly custom introspective system, I think using .info is your best bet as you can be guaranteed these collections can always be set.

Hmmm... I hear your concern about backref but I would plead for it, as I find it is an incredibly convenient declarative way to do relationships in both directions. But it's your choice obviously.

The only point I can try to argue is when you speak of the complexity of "trying to guess that both sides are viewonly", because in the case of the backref you would be constructing it yourself, not guessing; or if it's a backref() function, I get the impression one can check it pretty easily. Hmmm... would you be open to a PR?

> Hmmm... I hear your concern about backref but I would plead for it, as I find it is an incredibly convenient declarative way to do relationships in both directions. But it's your choice obviously.

as i said, backref() is not going away.

> 
> The only point I can try to argue is when you speak of the complexity of "trying to guess that both sides are viewonly", because in the case of the backref you would be constructing it yourself, not guessing; or if it's a backref() function, I get the impression one can check it pretty easily. Hmmm... would you be open to a PR?

a PR for...no warning with back_popualtes / backref and viewonly?  sorry, I'm opposed to that because I am triyng to ensure the rules for things are strict and consistent to as great a degree as is feasible.     I also don't have a clear rationale for the introspection use case either which as always can be performed on your end using the info dictionary.

Fair enough. Backref is going away in the view_only case, but I've already paid the cost and I'll live without it.
Regards

issue.title: warning on relationship(viewonly=True, backref(lazy="dynamic"))

labels.name: question
labels.description: issue where a "fix" on the SQLAlchemy side is unlikely, hence more of a usage question

issue.body:
On the commit 4376c2e, Adding a backref into a `viewonly` relationship was deprecated to avoid the issue where a backref one2many collection is modified, but the respective many2one relationship cannot be assigned.

However, if the `backref` is `lazy="dynamic"`, there is no risk of the collection in the one2many side of the relationship being modified in this case, so forgive me if I misunderstood the deprecation, but I think it is unwarranted in this specific case.

Conversely, if the `backref` is `lazy="select"` but both sides of the relationship are `viewonly`, then there should also be no harm, hence no warning, but you might consider this a separate issue.

Here is a simple example file showing the warning that I think is unwarranted (`.txt` added so it can be attached to a github issue):
[test_backref.py.txt](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/files/4429905/test_backref.py.txt)

issue.body: We have two complaints that the change in #5149 prevents the creation of two bidirectional viewonly relationships using the backref() function.      So we will propose new keyword argment viewonly_backref=backref() which explicitly sets up a relationship in the other direction as it does now, *except* that it doesn't set up the mutation events.   viewonly_back_populates will also be added to suit the case where the bidrectionality is set up in separate relationships however we still want the lazy loader to be able to use the many-to-one loader optimization case as well as having the two relationships be introspectable as related.
